const draft = `# Elm Quay Housing samlar anmälningar i en vy

Elm Quay Housings underhållsteam valde egna kategorier när det prövade Svale Systems i två hus under åtta veckor. Arbetsledaren Maya Lind beskriver erfarenheterna, och teamets interna anteckning sätter gränser för vad de uppmätta tiderna säger om programvaran.

Av [ditt namn]

Telefonanmälningar och mejl förvarades tidigare separat hos Elm Quay Housing, som förvaltar 640 lägenheter. I september 2025 beslutade det egna underhållsteamet att testa en gemensam reparationslogg så att personal på olika arbetspass skulle kunna se samma information.

## Teamet behåller telefonen för de boende

Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation. Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen. De boende kunde fortfarande anmäla reparationer per telefon.

– Vi ville att kvällspasset skulle se vad morgonpasset redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen, skriver underhållsteamets arbetsledare Maya Lind i en mejlintervju.

– Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att lägga in de första anmälningarna. Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa hus börjar.

## Mätningen omfattar 31 reparationsanmälningar

Bolagets interna anteckning från försöket, daterad den 4 december 2025, utesluter akuta ärenden och arbeten som beställts före testet. Den redovisar 31 registrerade reparationsanmälningar.

Mediantiden från anmälan till tilldelning var två arbetsdagar under försöket och tre under de föregående åtta veckorna. Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden.

Det saknas mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet och tiden tills reparationerna var färdiga. Siffrorna ger därmed inget underlag för slutsatser om dessa delar.

## Lind bedömer försöket inför nästa beslut

Försöket har ännu inte utökats. Teamet ska fatta beslut efter att ha kontrollerat hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer.

– Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen. Att ha en gemensam vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser, skriver Lind.

## Du kan läsa vidare om införandet

Kundfallet publiceras av leverantören Svale Systems. För dig som överväger ett eget försök finns [Svales checklista för införande](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist) att läsa.
`;

+# Source and quotation comparison: draft 1
+
+The complete supplied brief, source material, current draft and quotation guidance were read. Source language: English. Target language: Swedish. This comparison concerns source support and the meaning and idiomatic expression of translated quotations. It does not review general style or mechanics. Source passages below are quoted in their original language.
+
+Three findings remain: two source-support findings concerning the specificity of attribution, and one quotation-translation finding. The byline is an explicitly visible name placeholder and asserts no actual author's identity.
+
+## Complete claim accounting
+
+### 1. Title
+
+Draft: **“Elm Quay Housing samlar anmälningar i en vy”**.
+
+Source: **“In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.”** Also Lind: **“I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”**
+
+The title names the customer and the consolidated view of reports. Its journalistic present describes the case's action; the quotation itself also describes the view's benefit in the present. It does not assert an expansion or a company-wide implementation. No finding.
+
+### 2. Introductory summary: categories and customer agency
+
+Draft: **“Elm Quay Housings underhållsteam valde egna kategorier”**.
+
+Source: **“The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents.”** Also Lind: **“The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”**
+
+The team remains the acting party and the categories its own. “Valde” summarizes the team's choice involved in designing its own categories; it does not credit their design to Svale or claim that they came from a supplier template. The source's more specific account of design supports the less detailed summary of choosing. No finding.
+
+### 3. Introductory summary: trial, supplier, sites and duration
+
+Draft: **“när det prövade Svale Systems i två hus under åtta veckor.”**
+
+Source: **“In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.”** **“It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair.”** **“Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks.”**
+
+Svale Systems names the supplier's solution by ordinary metonymy in a sentence about trying it. The paragraph and body identify that solution as the repair log. Buildings and duration are preserved. This does not introduce a trial of other suppliers or an eight-week training period. No finding.
+
+### 4. Introductory summary: interviewee and experience
+
+Draft: **“Arbetsledaren Maya Lind beskriver erfarenheterna”**.
+
+Source: **“Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:”** followed by **“We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”**, **“We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”**, and **“I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”**
+
+The role, named interviewee and description of actual experience are supported. “Arbetsledaren” expresses the supervisory role without adding a gender. No finding in this introductory formulation.
+
+### 5. Introductory summary: source of the limitations
+
+Draft: **“och teamets interna anteckning sätter gränser för vad de uppmätta tiderna säger om programvaran.”**
+
+Source: **“Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.”**
+
+The limitations on interpreting the figures are supported, including the note's explicit refusal to attribute the difference to software. The draft changes the attribution from an internal note of Elm Quay to the maintenance team's internal note. The supplied package does not establish that narrower institutional ownership. Source-support finding S1 below.
+
+### 6. Byline
+
+Draft: **“Av [ditt namn]”**.
+
+Source brief: **“No author name supplied.”** The invocation supplies no additional author name. The commissioning writer's name is explicitly left as a placeholder under the resolved author rule.
+
+The bracketed text does not present an invented person as the author. “Ditt” addresses the user whose name is to replace the placeholder; it conveys no natural gender. No finding.
+
+### 7. Earlier reporting arrangement
+
+Draft: **“Telefonanmälningar och mejl förvarades tidigare separat hos Elm Quay Housing”**.
+
+Source: **“Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately.”** The preceding subject is **“Elm Quay Housing”** and its own maintenance team.
+
+The means of reporting, separate storage and earlier period are unchanged. “Förvarades” describes storage, not different departments or separate buildings. No finding.
+
+### 8. Customer's portfolio
+
+Draft: **“som förvaltar 640 lägenheter.”**
+
+Source: **“Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats.”**
+
+The subject, activity, count and object are preserved. The draft does not say the company owns the flats or that all 640 were included in the trial. No finding.
+
+### 9. Decision, timing, customer initiative and objective
+
+Draft: **“I september 2025 beslutade det egna underhållsteamet att testa en gemensam reparationslogg så att personal på olika arbetspass skulle kunna se samma information.”**
+
+Source: **“In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information.”**
+
+Month, year, decision-maker, company affiliation, shared repair log and intended access to the same information are preserved. “Så att ... skulle kunna” presents the team's purpose rather than claiming a measured outcome. The two-building scope was already supplied in the introduction. No finding.
+
+### 10. Telephone-reporting heading
+
+Draft: **“Teamet behåller telefonen för de boende”**.
+
+Source: **“The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents.”**
+
+“Telefonen” is an ordinary metonym for telephone reporting, as the paragraph below makes explicit. The historical narrative's present tense does not introduce a new claim that this channel remained open indefinitely after the trial. The team and resident access are preserved. No finding.
+
+### 11. Supplier selection and functional check
+
+Draft: **“Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation.”**
+
+Source: **“It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.”** Here “It” refers to the maintenance team introduced in the preceding sentences.
+
+The actor, supplier, sequence and tested capability are preserved. The wording reports testing whether the capability existed, rather than manufacturing a comparative ranking or an unqualified technical guarantee. Omitting the unavailable comparison adds no comparison. No finding.
+
+### 12. Supplier's implementation work and training
+
+Draft: **“Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen.”**
+
+Source: **“Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions.”**
+
+The supplier's activities and both counts are preserved. “Vid två tillfällen” expresses the two training sessions; it does not supply their duration or claim all employees were trained. No finding.
+
+### 13. Continued resident access by telephone
+
+Draft: **“De boende kunde fortfarande anmäla reparationer per telefon.”**
+
+Source: **“The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents.”**
+
+Keeping telephone reporting open supports residents' continued ability to report repairs that way during the trial. No claim is made about whether any particular resident used it or was satisfied. No finding.
+
+### 14. First quotation: shift objective
+
+Draft: **“– Vi ville att kvällspasset skulle se vad morgonpasset redan hade gjort.”**
+
+Source: **“We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done.”**
+
+The first-person plural, desired rather than measured visibility, respective shifts, and previously completed action are preserved. The Swedish collective shift nouns convey the same ordinary reference to staff working those shifts. No source-support or translation finding.
+
+### 15. First quotation: ownership and supplier assistance
+
+Draft: **“Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen”**.
+
+Source: **“The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”**
+
+Ownership stays with the customer group; Svale assists with putting the categories into the log. The quotation neither turns assistance into category design nor turns the customer into a passive beneficiary. Meaning, certainty and plain voice are preserved. No finding.
+
+### 16. Attribution of the first quotation
+
+Draft: **“skriver underhållsteamets arbetsledare Maya Lind i en mejlintervju.”**
+
+Source: **“Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:”** and **“All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided.”**
+
+The speaker, email medium and “skriver” attribution are supported. The supplied job title establishes supervision in maintenance, but it does not expressly establish that Lind leads this particular own maintenance team. The added genitive relationship “underhållsteamets” is a source-support finding, S2 below. No voice, location, emotion or remembered conversation is invented.
+
+### 17. Second quotation: relative effort
+
+Draft: **“– Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att lägga in de första anmälningarna.”**
+
+Source: **“We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports.”**
+
+The first-person group, relative duration, agreement on categories and limitation to the first reports are preserved. No actual number of hours or causal efficiency claim is added. “Lade mer tid” and “komma överens” are idiomatic expressions of the same experience. No finding.
+
+### 18. Second quotation: preparation recommendation
+
+Draft: **“Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa hus börjar.”**
+
+Source: **“I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”** Context: **“In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.”**, **“The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.”**
+
+The individual first-person assessment, conditional “would,” allocation of the category-agreement time and timing before the next building's start are all carried over. However, the absolute Swedish expression “nästa hus börjar” does not idiomatically identify what the building begins; it invites a physical construction reading and obstructs the intended start of the trial there. This is quotation-translation finding T1, rather than an invented source event.
+
+### 19. Count heading
+
+Draft: **“Mätningen omfattar 31 reparationsanmälningar”**.
+
+Source: **“Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”**
+
+The heading describes the report-count measurement explained immediately below. The exclusions are carried into the section. It does not expressly say every one of the 31 supplied an observed assignment interval or that the trial captured emergencies. Read in that context, its count and object are supported. No finding.
+
+### 20. Internal note, trial, date and exclusions
+
+Draft: **“Bolagets interna anteckning från försöket, daterad den 4 december 2025, utesluter akuta ärenden och arbeten som beställts före testet.”**
+
+Source: **“Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”**
+
+The body correctly identifies the company-level source, its internal and trial-related status, exact date, emergencies and the work ordered before the trial. “Akuta ärenden” expresses emergencies in the repair-report context. “Före testet” modifies when work was ordered, not when it was completed. No finding.
+
+### 21. Report count and attribution
+
+Draft: **“Den redovisar 31 registrerade reparationsanmälningar.”**
+
+Source: **“Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”**
+
+The preceding sentence supplies both exclusions; they apply to this count. “Registrerade” expresses entered reports, not completed repairs or satisfied residents. The count is attributed to the note. No finding.
+
+### 22. Assignment interval and comparison periods
+
+Draft: **“Mediantiden från anmälan till tilldelning var två arbetsdagar under försöket och tre under de föregående åtta veckorna.”**
+
+Source: **“Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software.”** The same note **“excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”**
+
+Median, interval endpoints, working-day unit, two and three, trial period and preceding eight-week period are preserved. “Tilldelning” retains assignment rather than repair completion. The surrounding section retains the exclusions and comparison caveat. No finding.
+
+### 23. Workloads and expressly withheld causal attribution
+
+Draft: **“Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden.”**
+
+Source: **“The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software.”**
+
+Both the actual workload difference and the note's expressly withheld causal attribution are preserved. The draft neither asserts software caused the difference nor asserts it definitely had no effect. It preserves whose non-attribution this is. No finding.
+
+### 24. Measurements not supplied
+
+Draft: **“Det saknas mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet och tiden tills reparationerna var färdiga.”**
+
+Source: **“There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.”**
+
+The three absent measurement categories are preserved. “Tiden tills reparationerna var färdiga” denotes completion time, while the preceding statistics remain assignment time. This sentence says measurements are absent; it does not claim cost savings, dissatisfaction, satisfaction, or a particular completion interval. No finding.
+
+### 25. Evidential conclusion about those dimensions
+
+Draft: **“Siffrorna ger därmed inget underlag för slutsatser om dessa delar.”**
+
+Source: **“Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period.”** **“There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.”**
+
+This is the writer's evidential conclusion based on the defined figures and missing measurements. It does not present an invented outcome, outside study or attributed customer opinion. “Dessa delar” refers to the three dimensions in the immediately preceding sentence. No finding.
+
+### 26. Assessment and next-decision heading
+
+Draft: **“Lind bedömer försöket inför nästa beslut”**.
+
+Source: **“Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures. The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.”**
+
+The heading characterizes the quoted personal assessment in the situation preceding the team's future decision. It does not say Lind alone makes that decision, that the decision has been taken, or that she recommends Svale universally. The subsequent quotation retains its reservation. No finding.
+
+### 27. Expansion status
+
+Draft: **“Försöket har ännu inte utökats.”**
+
+Source: **“The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.”**
+
+The negative assertion and “not yet” qualification are both supported. This is not an inference from silence. No finding.
+
+### 28. Future decision and its prerequisite
+
+Draft: **“Teamet ska fatta beslut efter att ha kontrollerat hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer.”**
+
+Source: **“The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.”**
+
+The deciding party, future modality, sequence, category check and larger-repair scope are preserved. The preceding sentence supplies expansion as the decision's referent. The draft does not assert that the category check has already occurred or will succeed. No finding.
+
+### 29. Final quotation: choice to repeat
+
+Draft: **“– Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen.”**
+
+Source: **“I would choose to do the trial again.”** Also: **“Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures.”**
+
+The first-person singular and conditional willingness to repeat are preserved. This remains Lind's own assessment rather than a conclusion generated from the measured interval. It does not become a universal recommendation or a commitment to expand. No finding.
+
+### 30. Final quotation: benefit and reservation
+
+Draft: **“Att ha en gemensam vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser, skriver Lind.”**
+
+Source: **“Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”** Also: **“The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information.”**, **“a shared repair log”**, and **“All interviews occurred by email”**.
+
+The shared, consolidated report view expresses the source's “one view” in its established shared-information context. The claimed benefit remains the speaker's and her group's experience; “men,” the individual conditional recommendation, an extra week, and preparation all survive. “Avsätta” idiomatically expresses leaving time available for preparation. “Skriver” accurately represents the email interview. No cost, completion-time or resident-satisfaction effect is added. No finding.
+
+### 31. Invitation heading
+
+Draft: **“Du kan läsa vidare om införandet”**.
+
+Source brief: **“The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.”**
+
+The reader is invited to read an implementation document. “Kan” keeps the step optional; it supplies no meeting, booking or trial. No finding.
+
+### 32. Publisher disclosure
+
+Draft: **“Kundfallet publiceras av leverantören Svale Systems.”**
+
+Source brief: **“The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems.”** Material: **“The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism.”**
+
+The publisher and supplier relationship are disclosed explicitly and accurately. Third-person narration and the disclosure do not claim independent publication. No finding.
+
+### 33. Linked next step and intended reader
+
+Draft: **“För dig som överväger ett eget försök finns [Svales checklista för införande](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist) att läsa.”**
+
+Source brief: **“Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems.”** **“The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.”**
+
+The address is conditional: it does not assert that an actual reader is considering a trial. The destination, document type, implementation purpose and action of reading match the supplied brief. “Svales” attributes the supplied supplier checklist in the context of the supplier's stated publication and its supplied /svale/ destination. No booking or product trial is substituted. No finding.
+
+## Pronoun, person, number and natural-gender accounting
+
+- **“det” in “när det prövade”** is third-person singular referring to the collective maintenance team. Swedish neuter grammatical gender follows “team”; it makes no assertion about team members' natural gender. The source likewise uses singular “team” and collective “It.”
+- **“det egna underhållsteamet”** contains the definite article and an ownership adjective, not a human neuter-gender assertion. “Own” is explicitly supplied in **“its own maintenance team”**; the company is the owner/affiliated organization.
+- **“Vi”** in the first and second quotations is first-person plural. **“We”** supplies both person and number. Its group is the customer's maintenance group in context; the draft does not invent a named membership list or a gender composition.
+- **“våra”** is first-person plural possession of plural categories, supported by **“ours”**. Its form agrees with the possessed categories and expresses no human natural gender.
+- **“oss”** in the first and last quotations is first-person plural object, supported by **“us”**. The customer's group remains the beneficiary. No singular self-reference, resident group or supplier group is substituted.
+- **“dem”** in the first quotation is third-person plural object referring to categories. The original **“them”** refers to the same plural categories. Neither supplies human natural gender.
+- **“Jag”** in the second and last quotations is first-person singular referring to Maya Lind. The original **“I”** independently supplies person and number; identifying Lind as referent is not needed to infer those features. The Swedish pronoun itself asserts no natural gender.
+- **“den tiden”** refers to the time for agreeing on categories, corresponding to **“that time”**. “Den” is a singular demonstrative with Swedish common grammatical gender from “tid,” not a natural-gender pronoun.
+- **“nästa hus”** is singular, matching **“the next building”**. The translation problem concerns the unspecified action with “börjar,” not number or gender.
+- **“Den redovisar”** is third-person singular referring to the internal note. “Den” has Swedish common grammatical gender from “anteckning”; its nonhuman referent remains the note, as the source's **“It”** does in **“It excludes emergencies”**. No female human referent is introduced.
+- **“de boende”** is the plural class of residents. **“residents”** and **“resident-satisfaction”** establish that population in context. “De” here forms a nominal expression and makes no assertion that a particular subset, number or natural gender participated.
+- **“de uppmätta tiderna,” “de första anmälningarna” and “de föregående åtta veckorna”** use plural definite articles, not human-gender pronouns. They agree with the measured intervals, first reports and preceding weeks already established.
+- **“Det saknas”** uses impersonal/expletive “det.” It does not identify a person, team or company, and is the Swedish construction for the source's **“There are no ... measurements.”**
+- **“dessa delar”** is a plural demonstrative referring to the immediately named cost, resident-satisfaction and completion-time dimensions. Those three dimensions are source-supported; the writer's evidential conclusion is accounted for separately above.
+- **“Du,” “dig,” “ditt” and “eget”** address one generic reader/user, respectively in the optional-reading invitation and visible byline placeholder. They add no natural-gender information and assert no actual reader behavior. The address is editorial rather than an attributed source quotation.
+- **“morgonpasset” and “kvällspasset”** are singular collective shift expressions; both languages use that collectivity. They do not turn an entire shift into one individual worker or assert any worker's gender.
+- **“arbetsledaren,” “medarbetare,” “personal” and the proper name “Maya Lind”** convey no additional natural gender in the Swedish draft. The source itself uses **“Her final quotation”**, but the draft supplies no “hon,” “hennes” or other human-gender claim. There is therefore no unsupported natural-gender inference from the name or job title.
+
+## Findings and smallest supported repairs
+
+### S1. Source support: the note is attributed specifically to the team
+
+Draft passage: **“teamets interna anteckning”** in the introduction.
+
+Source passage: **“Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered.”** The workload and causation qualifications attach to that note: **“The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software.”**
+
+What differs: the institution to which the source note is attributed. The material identifies the company's internal trial note. It does not establish an internal maintenance-team note or that the company note belongs specifically to that team. The body correctly uses **“Bolagets interna anteckning”**, but that does not remove the introductory narrowing.
+
+Concrete test, source true and draft false: Elm Quay's central operations analyst creates and retains an internal company trial note from the log records, independently of the maintenance team's own records. The note has the supplied date, count, exclusions and caveat. It is Elm Quay's internal trial note, but it is not the team's internal note. No supplied sentence excludes this arrangement. The source's **“its own maintenance team decided to trial”** establishes who initiated the trial, not ownership or authorship of the later note.
+
+Reverse test: a team-internal trial note within Elm Quay can also be the company's internal trial note. That direction has no necessary conflict; the defect is the unsupported narrower attribution, not denial of company affiliation.
+
+Smallest repair: **“bolagets interna anteckning”** in place of **“teamets interna anteckning”**. Keep the rest of the sentence and its justified limit on what the figures establish.
+
+### S2. Source support: an exact team-leadership relationship is added
+

## Findings and smallest supported repairs

### F1 — Source support: Elm Quay's organisational form

**Draft:** “bolagets interna anteckning” in the lead and “Bolagets interna anteckning från försöket” in the measurement section.

**Source:** “The customer, Elm Quay Housing”; “Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats”; “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025.” The brief's “operations managers at small housing companies” identifies the audience, not Elm Quay's legal or organisational form.

**Changed support:** “Bolag” names a company. The source identifies a customer housing organisation but supplies no such classification. This is factual background rather than an author's argument.

**Both-direction test:** A housing foundation or an unincorporated municipal housing service called Elm Quay Housing can manage 640 flats, have its own maintenance team and make this trial. Every supplied statement remains true, but “bolagets” misclassifies that organisation. No supplied statement excludes this case. Conversely, an actual company would satisfy both descriptions; the source's broader identification does not deny company status. There is no reverse-direction failure that establishes the narrower draft claim.

**Smallest repair:** Replace both instances with “Elm Quay Housings interna anteckning.” Preserve the remainder of each sentence.

### F2 — Source support: report entries become measurement coverage

**Draft:** “Mätningen omfattar 31 reparationsanmälningar.”

**Source:** “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period.”

**Changed support:** The supplied 31 is the note's count of entered reports. The heading of the section about measured assignment time instead gives the measurement a 31-report scope, without preserving the distinction between reports entered and reports contributing an assignment-time observation. The source supplies no denominator for that median.

**Both-direction test:** The log can contain the 31 entered reports counted by the note, with one still unassigned when the median is calculated from the remaining 30. The median can still be two working days, workloads can differ, and the listed exclusions can remain unchanged. No supplied statement says all entered reports were assigned or included in the time calculation, so none excludes this case. The entry count holds while a 31-report assignment-time measurement does not. In the reverse direction, measuring 31 reports cannot by itself establish the note's entry count: a different number of entries would distinguish those measures. A case in which the supplied note itself reports a different count is excluded by “says that 31 repair reports were entered”; this does not exclude the forward case.

**Smallest repair:** Use the heading “Anteckningen redovisar 31 reparationsanmälningar.” This retains the supplied number and its attribution without supplying a measurement sample size. The body already accurately calls them registered reports.

### F3 — Quotation translation: the next building's start is narrowed to a trial start

**Draft:** “Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan försöket börjar i nästa hus.”

**Source quotation:** “I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

**Relevant context:** “The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.”

**Changed meaning:** The translation makes the implicit activity an additional trial in the next building. The context establishes the repair-log work and the unresolved question of expansion, but not that the next building's eventual start must itself be a trial. This is an additive restriction on Lind's recommendation, rather than an idiomatic rearrangement. The first-person singular, conditional stance and reserved preparation time are otherwise faithfully preserved.

**Both-direction test:** After checking the categories, the team could decide to adopt the log routinely in a third building instead of treating that building as another trial. Lind's advice about setting aside category-agreement time before that building starts still applies; the draft's advice about a trial starting in it describes an event that need not occur. “The trial has not yet expanded” does not rule out that future decision, and no other supplied statement excludes the case. In the other direction, a trial starting in the next building would also be that building starting the activity; there is no narrower-to-broader failure that supplies the added trial identification.

**Smallest supported repair:** Remove the identification of that start as a trial. A translation retaining the settled repair-log referent is: “Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa hus börjar använda loggen.” The surrounding material settles the log as the activity; it does not settle the subtype “försöket.” Alternatively, paraphrase the established recommendation rather than resolve its ambiguity inside direct speech.

Other quotation translations preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive ordinary wording in idiomatic Swedish. No further translation finding is identified.
